transition.$description:
Tier 2 motion, part one. CSS has TWO motion properties and so does this file: `transition` interpolates between two states, `animation` runs a keyframed sequence. They are named property-first for the same reason colour is — the name tells you which declaration the token belongs in. `--animation-spin` would be a lie as `--transition-spin`; `infinite` cannot go in a `transition`.

The family is called motion; no token is prefixed `--motion-`, any more than a spacing token is prefixed `--foundations-`. (Do NOT put a file-level `$description` here: Style Dictionary treats the root key as a token node and it collides with the one in semantic/effect.json.)

fast.$description: Direct feedback on a small control — hover, focus, checked. 93 reads across 29 files; effectively the system default in practice. Promoted from tokens/primitive/effect.json, where `fast`/`base`/`slow` were always intent names sitting in the raw-value tier. Value unchanged.

base.$description: A change big enough to want to be watched — a panel resizing, a floating button arriving.

slow.$description: Larger spatial moves. Was 350ms — the ONE value this restructure changed, and deliberately. Value-neutrality is a rule for protecting things that RENDER, and nothing renders this: zero readers in hub components, zero in cb-fish, zero in air-exchange; its only two readers are the /foundations/motion swatch demonstrating it. Preserving 350ms would have meant an off-step in the tier-1 duration scale forever to protect a docs demo. The token stays because the ROLE is real and drawer/sheet work will want it — same reasoning as `background-brand-active`.

animation.$description: Tier 2 motion, part two — the keyframed half. These carry duration + easing + iteration but NOT the keyframes name, which is component-specific and stays with the component: `animation: esa-dropdown-fade var(--animation-enter);`. All 22 keyframed animations in the system hardcoded their timing before these existed, because the only motion tokens were composite `transition` strings that could not be used in an `animation` shorthand.

enter.$description: Small things arriving — dropdown, tooltip, popover, command palette.

exit.$description: The counterpart. Accelerating out is what makes a dismissal feel dismissed; reusing `enter` on the way out is the most common motion tell.

overlay-enter.$description: Large surfaces arriving — sheets, side dialogs, the snackbar, the search panel. Slower because they travel further, not because they matter more.

spin.$description: Continuous rotation — spinners, button loading states. Linear is not a default here, it is required: any easing on a loop reads as a stutter once per revolution.

indeterminate.$description: The progress-bar sweep, which travels and reverses, so it eases both ends.
